key_insight: Sparse, physics-constrained discovery identifies interpretable isotropic failure surfaces, with sharp Lode-angle dependence often more valuable than adding many terms.
engineering_relevance: The approach supports physically admissible yield and failure models from multiaxial tests and can reduce nominal-stress mapping bias through direct identification from structural loads.
method: Fit sparse invariant libraries enriched with isotropic cosine modes and learnable Podgorski–Bigoni–Piccolroaz atoms.
Compare convex-expert mixtures with competition or direction gates; enforce admissibility through construction or differentiable penalties.
Use differentiable ray-wise first roots and finite elements for end-to-end structural identification.
evidence_signal: Synthetic Mohr–Coulomb and PBP surfaces were recovered within 1% error; five experimental datasets were analysed, with PBP atoms reducing concrete fitting error fourfold.
watch_item: Convexity is guaranteed by construction for the competition gate, but library-based models rely on penalties and require careful admissibility checks.
paper_title: Sparse, admissible and interpretable: discovery of isotropic limit surfaces with extended invariant libraries, physically gated mixtures of experts, and end-to-end structural identification
